sources.README.md:
# Library sound restoration upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Ruby 2.7.0p0.
Dependencies: Ruby standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

sources.src/workflow.rb:
# Preservation sessions use block observers and distinct Struct visits.
Visit=Struct.new(:id,:file,:handle)
module Cancellation
 def cancel
  return if @aborted
  @aborted=true;@stop.call;@env.call('cancel',@file['token'],@number)
 end
end
class Attempt
 include Cancellation
 attr_reader :file,:number,:aborted
 def initialize(env,file,number,active=-> {1},audit=->(f){},view=->(f,o){})
  @env,@file,@number,@aborted=env,file,number,false;@stop=->{};env.call('transport',file['token'],number)
  if file['feed']
   callback=env.bind(->(packet){
    order=active.call;
    deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}
    value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']
   })
   env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
   @stop=-> {env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)};@stop.call if @aborted
  end
 end
end
class Session
 def initialize(env);@env=env;@visit=nil;@serial=0;@attempts=0;@tasks={};@disposed=false;end
 def current(v);@visit.equal?(v);end
 def enqueue(v,kind)
  @attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)
  h=Attempt.new(@env,v.file,n,->{0},->(frame){@env.call('recordProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})},->(frame,order){@env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame}) if current(v)});@tasks[n]=h;h
 end
 def notice(v,h);;@env.call('showQueued',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:h.number,visitId:v.id,status:'queued'});end
 def release(v);h=v.handle;v.handle=nil;h.cancel if h;end
 def select(file)
  return nil if @disposed
  @serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request
  v=Visit.new(request,file,nil);@visit=v;h=enqueue(v,'select');if current(v);v.handle=h;notice(v,h);else;h.cancel;end;h
 end
 def retry
  v=@visit;return nil if !v||!v.handle||@disposed
  v.handle.cancel
  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');if current(accepted);accepted.handle=h;else;h.cancel;end;notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted);h
 end
 def hide;@serial+=1;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old;end
 def dispose;return if @disposed;@disposed=true;hide;@tasks.each_value(&:cancel);end
 def snapshot;v=@visit;{visitId:v ? v.id : nil,fileId:v ? v.file['id'] : nil,attemptId:v&&v.handle ? v.handle.number : nil,disposed:@disposed,attempts:@attempts};end
end

class Telemetry
 attr_reader :stop
 def initialize(env,file)
  callback=env.bind(->(packet){deliver=->(frame){env.call('recordDelta',frame)};value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']})
  env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
  @stop=->{env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)}
 end
end

public_inputs.task:
A transfer with a warm progress source shows no initial progress until a later
packet arrives. Restore the initial progress update without changing the public
transfer, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, or queue-record behavior. Full
progress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the
current display backward. Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,
and subsequent uses.

limitations: Only TASK and the supplied public README.md and src/workflow.rb establish requirements. Automatic contracts, frozen experiences and evaluation observations are guidance.
Attempt 1 passed the reported syntax check and acceptance verdict. No behavioral observations establish complete correctness, causality or cross-task effectiveness.
README.md states: "A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion are outside this embedding's model." Adapter exception behavior is unspecified.
An older completion need not be suppressed merely because a newer packet is still decoding. The documented requirement prevents rollback after a newer frame has been displayed.
Provisional handles, generation counters and sequence counters are implementation options, not required public interfaces.

rules.body:
Apply when progress reception serves distinct visits and physical attempts, startup can emit synchronously, decoding may finish later, and audit and presentation have different lifetimes. README.md: "Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit." README.md: "The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order." Confirm these premises before transferring this guidance.

Install panel reception before starting the source, while preserving subsequent streaming and source reuse. Original src/workflow.rb: "env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)". Guard admission using the originating subscription and visit, including during startup before the outer caller receives its handle. README.md: "One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle." Retirement must prevent subsequent admission without relying solely on eventual physical cleanup.

Bind accepted decoding to its originating file, attempt and visit. Preserve its audit effect when decoding completes, including after cancellation or retirement, then recheck visit eligibility before visible publication. Original src/workflow.rb: "deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}" and "->(frame,order){@env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame}) if current(v)}". README.md: "recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel." Because audit callbacks may navigate synchronously, an admission-time validity check cannot replace the publication-time check. Already accepted decoding is not automatically ineligible for display solely because retry canceled its attempt while the visit remains current.

Where the task explicitly requires protection against out-of-order full frames, capture reception order before decoding and retain a publication watermark for the visit, spanning its retries. Publish an eligible completion only if it cannot replace a newer frame already displayed. Commit the watermark before invoking callback-capable presentation so reentrant publication cannot restore older authority. TASK: "Full\nprogress frames may decode out of order; do not allow an older frame to roll the\ncurrent display backward." Compare reception order rather than numeric progress: README.md states, "A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset." Continue auditing suppressed older completions.

Establish cleanup ownership before callback-capable startup, remove captured old ownership before cancellation, and recheck authority after callbacks. An older startup must clean its own retired resources without overwriting newer navigation. Original src/workflow.rb: "@serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request". Preserve removal commitment and idempotence: README.md states, "Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred." Keep cancellation and disposal independent for each workspace.

Keep an accepted retry bound to its entry visit across cancellation callbacks. Cancel the prior handle before enqueueing; preserve its one queue record and transfer construction even if cancellation navigates; cancel the resulting transfer if its visit ended and suppress retired queued notices. Original src/workflow.rb: "v.handle.cancel\n  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');if current(accepted);accepted.handle=h;else;h.cancel;end;notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted);h". Preserve queue recording before transfer construction and existing counters. Original src/workflow.rb: "@attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)".

Keep freshness filtering specific to the panel requirement; do not transfer it to unrelated consumers or tasks without supporting evidence. Preserve public queue and notice fields and adapter interfaces. README.md: "Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size." No separate authorization is supplied. Preserve diagnostic behavior, including its existing startup sequence: README.md states, "The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance."

Verify cached startup and later streaming; immediate and deferred decoding; newer completion followed by older completion with both audits retained; and a later-received lower loaded value replacing an earlier display. Verify freshness across retries and reentrant publication, including navigation during recordProgress. During startup, hide, switch or reopen from showProgress and emit further packets before startup returns: retired admission must stop, accepted audits must remain, and newer ownership must survive. Exercise navigation during cancellation and listener removal, accepted entry-bound retries, current queued notices, same-file reopening, repeated cleanup, disposal, workspace independence, unchanged record shapes and unchanged Telemetry behavior. TASK: "Preserve ordinary streaming, diagnostic telemetry,\nand subsequent uses."

checkpoints: Verify cached synchronous startup progress and subsequent streamed progress.
Complete newer frames before older frames; verify that older completions retain audit history without replacing newer displayed frames.
Verify that a later-arriving full frame with a lower loaded value can replace an earlier frame.
Navigate or hide from showProgress during startup, then emit additional packets before startup returns; verify retirement, cleanup, and continued operation of the new visit.
Complete accepted decoding after hide, replacement, retry, or disposal; verify retained audit and appropriate display eligibility.
Reenter navigation from listener removal and cancellation; verify that newer navigation retains ownership.
Verify accepted retries remain associated with their entry visit, preserve queue records, and cancel their resulting transfer if that visit has ended.
Verify repeated cleanup, same-file reopening, independent workspaces, unchanged queue and notice shapes, and unchanged diagnostic telemetry.
forbidden_effects: Missing cached initial panel progress because listening begins after start.
Allowing an older full frame to replace a newer frame already displayed in the same visit.
Treating numeric loaded values as a monotonic freshness measure.
Discarding audit work already accepted before retirement or cancellation.
Publishing progress or queued notices for a retired visit, including after reopening the same file.
Allowing an older startup or cleanup operation to overwrite or remove resources owned by newer navigation.
Changing diagnostic telemetry startup, decoding, delta recording, or cleanup behavior.
Adding byteCount or otherwise changing queue-record fields.
lifecycle_identity: Each selection creates a distinct visit, including selection of the identical file object.
Retry creates a new physical attempt within the existing visit.
Progress audit remains associated with the file and attempt that accepted the packet; visible progress belongs to its originating visit.
The progress source is shared across attempts and visits for a file; file object identity, id, and size are stable.
Attempt numbering and disposal state belong to each Session instance.

obligations.text: Make the panel subscription available before starting a source that can synchronously emit cached packets, while preserving later streaming and subsequent source reuse.
Retain audit recording for each accepted packet when decoding completes, immediately or later, including completion after its visit closes or its attempt is canceled.
Publish a decoded frame only while its originating visit remains current. Recheck eligibility after recordProgress, because that synchronous host callback can navigate.
Order panel frames by packet reception rather than decode completion or numeric loaded value. Once a newer frame has been displayed in a visit, an older completion must not replace it.

Support retirement during synchronous startup before the caller receives the cleanup handle: prevent further packet admission by the retired subscription, retain accepted audit work, and clean up the eventual retired resources.

Preserve newer navigation through callback-capable cleanup. Retire captured old ownership before cancellation and prevent an outer operation from overwriting resources installed by reentrant navigation.

Preserve retry acceptance behavior: cancel the prior handle before enqueueing, then enqueue and record exactly one retry for the captured visit even if cancellation navigates. Cancel the resulting handle if that visit is no longer current, and emit its queued notice only while it is current.
Preserve synchronous queue recording before transfer construction, existing queue and notice fields, attempt numbering, transport calls, and cancellation behavior.
Preserve listener-removal commitment before detach callbacks, inert repeated removal, idempotent cancellation and disposal, disposal of tracked transfers, and independence between workspaces.
Keep the Telemetry consumer's existing live delta behavior and public source/sink interfaces unchanged.

ordering_barriers: Panel reception must be installed before start can emit cached packets.
Capture packet ordering and originating identity before invoking decode, which can complete immediately or later.
Audit accepted decoding before attempting visible publication; recheck current-visit eligibility after the audit callback.
Prevent older publication after a newer frame is displayed, including reentrant publication through synchronous host callbacks.
Clear current old-visit ownership before callback-capable cancellation; recheck the selection request after old cleanup.
A retry cancels its previous handle before its retained enqueue operation.
Record the queue entry before constructing the corresponding Attempt.
Commit listener removal before invoking the host detach callback.
preservation: Ordinary streaming, subsequent uses, transport creation, retry, navigation, cleanup, audit, and queue-record behavior.
Accepted decoding survives physical listener removal; cancellation does not retroactively remove retained history.
Existing queue records contain exactly fileId, attemptId, visitId, and kind; notices contain fileId, attemptId, visitId, and status set to queued.
Current-visit display eligibility is distinct from attempt cancellation: accepted work is not automatically made invisible merely because retry canceled its attempt.
Full frames replace displayed state and may decrease or reset loaded values.
Telemetry retains its existing start-before-listen sequence and recordDelta behavior.
scope: Draft contract for restoring initial panel progress and preventing stale decoded frames from rolling back its display in src/workflow.rb.
Normative evidence consists only of TASK and the supplied public README.md and src/workflow.rb.
This stage produces structured analysis without modifying files.

# Library sound restoration upload

This workspace selects payload files, starts transfers, records queue and
progress history, and paints progress for its open panel. Runtime: Ruby 2.7.0p0.
Dependencies: Ruby standard library. See src for the session/component entry API.

Selecting a file creates a visit. Retry replaces the physical attempt without
opening another visit. Selecting the same file object again opens a new visit.
The source is shared by attempts and visits for that file. start may emit cached
packets synchronously; decoding yields a full frame, immediately or later.
Decode completion order can differ from packet arrival order.

recordProgress appends transfer history; showProgress paints the open panel.
Queue records, notices, cancellation, retry, navigation, and cleanup retain
their existing behavior. Queue records are {fileId, attemptId, visitId, kind}
unless a separate authorization adds byteCount from file.size.

One startup window is relevant to this maintenance request: start may emit
more than one packet synchronously. A showProgress callback may select or hide
another visit before start returns, while its caller has not yet received the
returned cleanup handle.

The same source service also has a diagnostic consumer, Telemetry/
collectProgressTelemetry, whose existing live delta observations are separate
from the panel. Keep its existing behavior during this maintenance.
Removing a listener commits removal before calling the host detach callback;
that callback may synchronously select, hide or dispose. Repeated removal is
inert. Host callbacks execute synchronously unless explicitly deferred.

Files have stable object identity and immutable id/size during these commands.
A full frame replaces displayed state; loaded values can decrease or reset.
A decode result resolves once; rejected decode and physical transfer completion
are outside this embedding's model. Each workspace has its own lifetime.

Environment.call/bind provides a synchronous source embedding: listen(file
 token, callback token) returns a subscription, start can invoke it before
returning, and unlisten may reenter navigation. decode(file token, packet,
completion token) returns {deferred:false,frame} or {deferred:true}. Deferred
completion invokes the bound native closure on an explicit later host turn.
Transport receives a physical cancellation observer corresponding to the
native attempt state; cancel is idempotent. The wire embedding interns file
objects and forwards source/sink calls. Go uses context cancellation; the other
native ports use object flags. No native DOM/Promise runtime is claimed.

# Preservation sessions use block observers and distinct Struct visits.
Visit=Struct.new(:id,:file,:handle,:received,:displayed,:generation)
module Cancellation
 def cancel
  return if @aborted
  @aborted=true;@stop.call;@env.call('cancel',@file['token'],@number)
 end
end
class Attempt
 include Cancellation
 attr_reader :file,:number,:aborted
 def initialize(env,file,number,active=-> {1},audit=->(f){},view=->(f,o){})
  @env,@file,@number,@aborted=env,file,number,false;@stop=->{}
  yield self if block_given?
  env.call('transport',file['token'],number)
  if file['feed'] && !@aborted
   callback=env.bind(->(packet){
    next if @aborted
    order=active.call;
    next unless order
    deliver=->(frame){ audit.call(frame);view.call(frame,order)}
    value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']
   })
   subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
   removed=false
   @stop=-> {unless removed;removed=true;env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription);end}
   if @aborted;@stop.call;else;env.call('start',file['token']);end
  end
 end
end
class Session
 def initialize(env);@env=env;@visit=nil;@serial=0;@attempts=0;@tasks={};@disposed=false;end
 def current(v);@visit.equal?(v);end
 def enqueue(v,kind)
  v.generation=(v.generation||0)+1;generation=v.generation
  @attempts+=1;n=@attempts;entry={fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,visitId:v.id,kind:kind};;@env.call('record',entry)
  h=Attempt.new(@env,v.file,n,
   ->{if current(v) && v.generation==generation;v.received=(v.received||0)+1;end},
   ->(frame){@env.call('recordProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})},
   ->(frame,order){
    if current(v) && order>(v.displayed||0)
     v.displayed=order
     @env.call('showProgress',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:n,frame:frame})
    end
   }) do |attempt|
    @tasks[n]=attempt
    v.handle=attempt if current(v) && v.generation==generation
   end
  h.cancel unless current(v) && v.generation==generation
  h
 end
 def notice(v,h);;@env.call('showQueued',{fileId:v.file['id'],attemptId:h.number,visitId:v.id,status:'queued'});end
 def release(v);h=v.handle;v.handle=nil;h.cancel if h;end
 def select(file)
  return nil if @disposed
  @serial+=1;request=@serial;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old
  return nil if @disposed||@serial!=request
  v=Visit.new(request,file,nil);@visit=v;h=enqueue(v,'select');notice(v,h) if current(v)&&v.handle.equal?(h);h
 end
 def retry
  v=@visit;return nil if !v||!v.handle||@disposed
  release(v)
  accepted=v;h=enqueue(accepted,'retry');notice(accepted,h) if current(accepted)&&accepted.handle.equal?(h);h
 end
 def hide;@serial+=1;old=@visit;@visit=nil;release(old) if old;end
 def dispose;return if @disposed;@disposed=true;hide;@tasks.each_value(&:cancel);end
 def snapshot;v=@visit;{visitId:v ? v.id : nil,fileId:v ? v.file['id'] : nil,attemptId:v&&v.handle ? v.handle.number : nil,disposed:@disposed,attempts:@attempts};end
end

class Telemetry
 attr_reader :stop
 def initialize(env,file)
  callback=env.bind(->(packet){deliver=->(frame){env.call('recordDelta',frame)};value=env.call('decode',file['token'],packet,env.bind(deliver));deliver.call(value['frame']) unless value['deferred']})
  env.call('start',file['token']);subscription=env.call('listen',file['token'],callback)
  @stop=->{env.call('unlisten',file['token'],subscription)}
 end
end
